assignmentHtml.task: Research Apache Pinot's architecture. Investigate: (1) ingestion — Kafka consumer, real-time tables, batch, CDC handling with rewrites; (2) updates/deletes — segment optimization, deletes file, primary index, real-time table indexing, how late/out-of-order events are handled; (3) joins — dimension tables, segment pruning; (4) multi-tenant isolation — users, projects, resource groups, quota; (5) recovery — controller, ZooKeeper, Helix, what is restored; (6) license — Apache 2.0; (7) version caveats. Note whether Pinot is primarily serving or supports transformation.
assignmentHtml.context: Evidence cutoff 2026-09-16. Open-source analytics platform investigation. Requirements: clickstream 3TB/day, mutable orders CDC, Iceberg lake, multi-tenant, erasure, recovery. Only OSS editions.
assignmentHtml.expected_output: Structured dossier section for Apache Pinot covering all topics with source URLs.

answerHtml: Apache Pinot OSS dossier compiled across ingestion, updates/deletes, joins, multi-tenancy, recovery, license, and version caveats. Key findings: (1) Pinot is primarily a serving OLAP engine — it supports limited ingestion-level transformations (Groovy/scalar functions) but is not an ETL/ELT tool. (2) Iceberg lake integration is not available in OSS Pinot — it is a StarTree commercial feature; Pinot's deep store supports S3/GCS/ADLS/HDFS/local. (3) 'Deletes file' is an Iceberg concept; Pinot OSS uses queryableDocIds/validDocIds bitmaps plus Minion compaction tasks. (4) Multi-tenant isolation exists via tenants (server/broker tags), workload budgets (1.4.0+), per-table QPS quotas, and broker RLS filters — but there are no 'users', 'projects', or 'resource groups' as named entities; those map to tenant tags + workload configs + quotas. (5) Recovery: ZooKeeper holds all cluster metadata; restore ZK snapshot + restart controllers; servers re-download segments from the deep store. (6) License: Apache 2.0 confirmed. (7) Version caveats include null-semantics changes in upcoming release, HEAP→MMAP default in 1.4.0, removed pre-1.0 APIs, and known 1.3.0 multi-stream Kafka bug.

evidence.snippet: Four node types: Controller, Broker, Server, Minion. Real-time ingest: controller assigns servers as direct consumers; consuming segments accumulate in memory, immediately queryable, flushed to disk as completed segments. Offline ingest: jobs transform raw data into segments, pushed to deep store, servers download. Helix manages cluster state; ZooKeeper stores controller leader, servers/brokers, tables, segments.
evidence.supports: Architecture overview: components, real-time vs offline ingestion paths, Helix/ZooKeeper roles

evidence.snippet: Primary key defined via primaryKeyColumns; comparisons use timeColumn by default or upsertConfig.comparisonColumn. Out-of-order records either persisted-but-invalid (default) or dropped via dropOutOfOrderRecord=true. Partial upsert REALTIME only; partial upsert skips out-of-order events entirely. commit-time compaction via enableCommitTimeCompaction removes dead tuples at segment flush.
evidence.supports: Updates/deletes: primary index mechanism, real-time indexing in consuming segment, late/out-of-order event handling, commit-time compaction

evidence.snippet: Point deletes track queryableDocIds separately from validDocIds (soft-delete). deletedKeysTTL removes metadata for deleted keys after TTL window. UpsertCompactionTask physically rewrites segments using snapshotted validDocIds, reclaiming ~90% storage. PK→distinct-segment-count tracking prevents resurrection of deleted keys during restart. Requires Minion scheduler.
evidence.supports: Deletes mechanism in detail: soft deletes, metadata TTL, physical compaction, consistency safeguards

evidence.snippet: Segment compaction replaces completed segments with compacted versions containing only latest record versions. validDocIdsType config: SNAPSHOT (default), SNAPSHOT_WITH_DELETE, IN_MEMORY, IN_MEMORY_WITH_DELETE. If a completed segment contains only old records, it is deleted immediately. Thresholds: invalidRecordsThresholdPercent, invalidRecordsThresholdCount. bufferTimePeriod delays compaction.
evidence.supports: Segment optimization via upsert compaction: thresholds, delete-aware snapshots, immediate deletion of fully-invalid segments

evidence.snippet: Offline upsert keeps row with greatest comparison value; defaults to timeColumn if comparisonColumns unset. Must define primaryKeyColumns. FULL upsert only; PARTIAL REALTIME only. TransformConfigs can generate missing comparison columns via now(). Changing primaryKey or comparisonColumns requires full rebuild.
evidence.supports: Offline (batch) upsert behavior, comparison logic, limitations

evidence.snippet: CDC with Debezium: ExtractNewRecordState flattens envelope; delete.handling.mode: rewrite adds __deleted field mapped to deleteRecordColumn. upsertConfig.mode FULL or PARTIAL (OVERWRITE/IGNORE strategies). comparisonColumns resolves out-of-order events. UpsertCompactionTask scheduled via Minion with invalidRecordsThresholdPercent/count thresholds. deletedKeysTTL recommended for retention.
evidence.supports: CDC handling: Debezium transforms, tombstone mapping, upsert modes, compaction scheduling

evidence.snippet: Dimension tables replicate all segments to every server in the tenant, loaded into in-memory hash map keyed by primary key for constant-time lookups. Cluster-level max size 200MB (controller.dimTable.maxSize). Uses allservers assignment strategy. LOOKUP UDF (single-stage) or lookupJoinStrategy (multi-stage). Segment refresh REPLACES entire segment. No time-based partitioning, no incremental updates, no row-level updates.
evidence.supports: Joins: dimension table replication, in-memory lookup, segment refresh semantics, limitations

evidence.snippet: Colocated joins require both tables partitioned identically (same function, count, server assignment, join-on-partition-key equality). Runs without shuffling. Broker-side partition pruning can remove partition classes when every table in group prunes them. Empty partitions keep aligned workers; class removed only when no table has data for it.
evidence.supports: Joins: colocated join strategy, partition-class semantics, broker pruning integration

evidence.snippet: Broker-side pruning: time pruner (requires primary time column) and partition pruner (Modulo/Murmur/FNV/HashCode/ByteArray/BoundedColumnValue). Server-side: column min/max stats, bloom filters (IN ≤10 values). MSE supports useBrokerPruning; default logical planner path applies pruning on physical optimizer path. Metrics: numSegmentsPrunedByBroker, numSegmentsQueried, numSegmentsProcessed.
evidence.supports: Segment pruning: broker-side (time/partition), server-side (min/max, bloom), multi-stage support, monitoring

evidence.snippet: Every table bound to server tenant + broker tenant via text tags ({tenant}_OFFLINE/_REALTIME/_BROKER). Tables only scheduled on hardware with matching tag. Created via POST /tenants with tenantRole, tenantName, numberOfInstances, offlineInstances, realtimeInstances. Co-location allowed (same server can hold _OFFLINE and _REALTIME tags). No separate 'users'/'projects' concepts—tenant tags enforce data/resource isolation.
evidence.supports: Multi-tenant isolation: tenant tagging model, instance tagging, no users/projects entities

evidence.snippet: Two isolation layers: infrastructure (tenant tags) + data (row-level filtering, tenantId sorted column). Workload-based query isolation via workloadName option with CPU ns/memory bytes budgets. Broker-level query quotas (maxQueriesPerSecond). RLS at broker: pinot.broker.access.control.principals.*.tables/rls. Single-table approach with tenantId sorted column for near-instant pruning.
evidence.supports: Multi-tenant: combined infrastructure + data isolation, row-level security, workload isolation, quotas

evidence.snippet: Introduced 1.4.0. QueryWorkloadConfig stored in ZK under /CONFIGS/QUERYWORKLOAD. Per-workload cpuCostNs + memoryCostBytes for brokerNode and serverNode. PropagationScheme splits budget across instances serving tables or tenants. Enforcement at server admission: queries rejected with SERVER_RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED when budget exhausted; in-flight queries not killed. Default enforcement window 60s. Requires thread CPU/memory sampling enabled. Controller computes and pushes per-instance budgets.
evidence.supports: Resource groups/budgets: workload-based isolation, CPU-memory budgets, propagation, enforcement mechanics

evidence.snippet: Three quota layers: table (tableConfig.maxQueriesPerSecond), database (databaseMaxQueriesPerSecond, per-db override), application (applicationMaxQueriesPerSecond, set via SET applicationName). Applied in order: application → database → table. Exceeded quota returns 429. Quotas split evenly across brokers serving the table.
evidence.supports: Quotas: per-table, per-database, per-application QPS limits, enforcement order

evidence.snippet: ZooKeeper state: Pinot stores all cluster metadata (table configs, schemas, segment assignments, ideal state) in ZK. Back up via ZK native snapshot or zkCopy. Disaster recovery: restore ZK snapshot, restart controllers to restore cluster metadata. Deep store is authoritative segment copy (S3/GCS/HDFS). Servers auto-re-download lost segments on startup or forceDownload=true. controller.startup.continueWithoutDeepStore=true avoids fail-fast on deep-store boot check. Table configs/schemas should live in version control.
evidence.supports: Recovery: ZK metadata backup/restore, deep store as authoritative data source, controller startup behavior

evidence.snippet: apache/pinot is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. A permissive license requiring preservation of copyright and license notices, with express grant of patent rights from contributors.
evidence.supports: License: Apache License 2.0 confirmed directly from repository

evidence.snippet: Positioned as 'an open-source distributed OLAP database for user-facing and agent-facing real-time analytics,' delivering 'sub-second queries on fresh data at petabyte scale' with 'hundreds of thousands of concurrent queries per second.' Features emphasize serving interactive dashboards, metrics APIs, and AI backends (RAG/decision engines). No mention of ETL/ELT or transformation pipelines.
evidence.supports: Pinot is primarily a serving engine; transformation support is limited to ingestion-level functions only

evidence.snippet: Ingestion-level transformations support: Groovy functions (must be enabled via controller.disable.ingestion.groovy=false) and registered scalar functions (DateTime, JSON json_format, Geospatial ST_*, H3). Three types: filtering (filterConfigs), column transformation (transformConfigs), and flattening (UNNEST at query time). REALTIME tables restricted to IMMUTABLE functions; OFFLINE allows any volatility. TransformConfigs can generate missing comparison columns via now(). Cannot mix Groovy and built-in functions in one transform.
evidence.supports: Transformation support: ingestion-level only (Groovy + built-in scalar functions), not a data pipeline/ETL tool

evidence.snippet: Upcoming release: group-by null handling changes (SQL NULL groups), multi-value aggregations skip nulls, singular livebrokers endpoint removed, legacy valid-docID REST endpoints removed, pre-1.0 Java/plugin APIs removed (NoSuchMethodError for stale plugins), TimeFieldSpec rejected in REST schema APIs, 12 deprecated controller config constants removed. 1.4.0: controller exits startup if table lacks TableConfig/Schema; loadMode default HEAP→MMAP; Avro logical types auto-handled. 1.3.0: multi-stream Kafka ingestion known bug not production-ready. 1.2.0: column-major segment builder default on; upsertConfig.consistencyMode introduced.
evidence.supports: Version caveats: behavior changes, deprecations, new defaults across recent releases

evidence.snippet: Query schedulers: fcfs (default), bounded_fcfs (per-table resource groups with threads_per_query_pct=20%, table_threads_soft_limit_pct=30%, table_threads_hard_limit_pct=45%), tokenbucket. Binary Workload Scheduler (1.3.0): primary (unbounded production) vs secondary (constrained ad-hoc) workloads. query_runner_threads/query_worker_threads dynamically adjustable via Helix without restart.
evidence.supports: Resource groups: bounded schedulers with per-table thread limits, token bucket, binary workload scheduler

evidence.snippet: Hybrid tables combine REALTIME (fresh, last hours) + OFFLINE (batch-corrected historical) under one logical table via time boundary = max end time across offline segments. Broker routes by time range. Overlapping real-time segments dropped by retention manager on offline push. Requires identical schemaName/tableNames; contiguous offline segments; real-time retention ≥ 2× batch interval. Pitfall: time gap in offline data stops boundary advancement and causes real-time data loss when retention expires.
evidence.supports: Late/batch-correction pattern: hybrid tables for Lambda architecture, time boundary routing, gap pitfalls

evidence.snippet: Upsert Compact Merge Task (1.3.0+, improved in 1.4.0) merges small upsert segments: two-phase cleanup (upload merged segments first, delete originals with validDocIDCount=0 after commit cycle). Requires upsertConfig.snapshot ≠ DISABLE. All merged segments must share partition. Prerequisites: Minion cluster running.
evidence.supports: Segment optimization: merging reduces segment count while compacting; two-phase safe cleanup
